children: Indian shares opened little changed on Tuesday as stronger-than-expected domestic growth data offset worries from rising crude oil prices driven by fresh escalation in Middle East tensions.
fell 0.17% to 24,039.75 and the BSE Sensex
shed 0.1% to 76,884.91 as of 9:22 a.m. IST.
Twelve of the 16 major sectors logged losses. Bank index
fell 1%, about 560 points, reversing the roughly 500-point gain it recorded in the closing auction session on Monday.
India's economy expanded 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, blowing past forecasts as an investment boom and manufacturing strength added to already-solid consumer demand.
The upside surprise for Asia's third-largest economy was offset by a rise in crude prices driven by geopolitical tensions from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

U.S. President Donald Trump threatened further strikes against Iran on Monday, while Iran launched missiles overnight at two U.S. air bases in Jordan in response to a U.S. attack on Iran's Larak Island.
